# Neural Gauge Scheduling for Certified Ellipsoidal Reach Tubes

**Working title:** *Learning the gauge, not the bound: amortized tightening of certified ellipsoidal reachability with structural soundness.*

**Authors:** [TBD]
**Version:** pure-Python (no MATLAB); every number regenerated by `paper-5/reproduce.sh`.

---

## 1. The idea (and why it is new)

Ellipsoidal reach tubes carry a **continuous gauge freedom that zonotopes, polytopes, and
normotopes do not have.** For the one-step external Minkowski sum of the propagated set with the
disturbance, the whole family

  Q_β = (1 + 1/β)·(A Q Aᵀ) + (1 + β)·Q_W ,  **β > 0**

is a **sound outer bound of `(A·E) ⊕ W` for *every* β>0** (it dominates the true support in every
direction; `App. A`). Over a horizon, the schedule `{β_1,…,β_N}` is a gauge: *any* positive schedule
yields a valid outer reach tube, but different schedules give different tightness. The classical
Kurzhanski–Varaiya (KV) rule fixes β **myopically** — tight along one preset direction each step.

**Our contribution:** treat the gauge schedule as a control variable and **learn a policy
`β_θ(features)` — a small neural network whose output passes through a softplus, so β>0 always — that
schedules the gauge to minimize a *global* objective (final-set log-volume), trained across many
systems.** Two properties make this more than "another learned-reachability method":

1. **Soundness is a hard structural invariant.** The tube is a valid outer bound for *any* network
   weights θ (Theorem 1). Learning only moves within the gauge freedom; it can change *tightness* but
   can **never** break soundness. Safety is certified *by construction*, decoupled from the learned
   component — unusual among learned reachability methods.
2. **It is ellipsoid-specific.** The scalar gauge β (equivalently the KV regularizer π(t) and the
   internal-tube rotation S(t)) is a feature of the *ellipsoidal* representation. Zonotope/polytope
   template methods choose *directions*; they have no continuous shape-evolution gauge to learn. So
   this mechanism cannot be reproduced by the adaptive-polytope / PCA-template / normotope-DP lines.

This directly answers the three seed questions: (1) mixing tubes that touch from different directions
= the policy allocating/scheduling the direction-and-gauge family; (2) an NN regulating the free
parameters of the ellipsoidal approximation, i.e. *neural control of a population of gauge schedules*;
(3) a new architecture — the differentiable gauge-tube step is a **layer**, and the policy-over-tube
stack is the architecture.

## 2. Theory

**Theorem 1 (structural soundness).** *For any β>0, `E_β := E(A q + q_W, Q_β)` satisfies
`(A·E) ⊕ W ⊆ E_β`. Hence for any policy `β_θ`, the rollout tube is a valid outer reachable-set
over-approximation, for every θ.*
*Proof.* For any direction `d`, `ρ(E_β,d)² − (ρ(A·E,d)+ρ(W,d))² = (p₁/√β − p₂√β)² ≥ 0` with
`p₁=√(dᵀAQAᵀd)`, `p₂=√(dᵀQ_W d)` (`App. A`). So `ρ(E_β,d) ≥ ρ((A·E)⊕W,d)` in every direction; a
convex set is contained in another iff its support is dominated everywhere. Softplus gives β>0 for
any θ, so the invariant holds for all weights. ∎

**Corollary (amortized optimality).** Minimizing final-set volume over the gauge schedule is a
well-posed optimal-control problem; `β_θ` amortizes its solution across a system distribution while
Theorem 1 keeps every rollout sound.

## 3. Experiments (`reproduce.sh`)

2-D LTI systems `x_{k+1}=A x_k+w`, rotation-scaling `A` (spectral radius 0.85–0.95), anisotropic
disturbance (condition 4–40, random orientation), horizon N=8. Objective: final-set log-volume.

**(a) The gauge is exploitable** (`gauge_gap.csv`). Per-instance optimizing the β-schedule vs. the
myopic KV choice: **mean volume ratio (myopic / optimized) = 1.44×** over 20 systems — a ~44% tighter
certified enclosure at *zero* soundness cost, purely from scheduling the gauge.

**(b) A learned policy amortizes it** (`amortized.csv`). A small MLP gauge policy (`ell_gauge.GaugePolicy`,
~60 params) trained on 40 systems and evaluated on **40 held-out systems**:
- beats myopic on **68%** of unseen systems;
- **mean volume ratio (myopic / policy) = 1.60×**, median **1.10×** (skewed: large wins on
  high-anisotropy systems, modest elsewhere — reported honestly);
- **captures 48% of the myopic→per-instance-oracle volume gap** in a *single forward pass* (no
  per-instance optimization) — the amortization claim, measured against the oracle on the *same* set.

**(c) Soundness holds for the learned schedule** (`soundness.csv`). Monte-Carlo containment of true
trajectories in the learned-policy tube: **min 1.0000** across test systems — as guaranteed by
Theorem 1, independent of θ. Four soundness unit-tests (`oracle_tests/test_ell_gauge.py`) verify the
gauge step dominates `(A·E)⊕W` in all directions for arbitrary β, and that the policy always emits β>0.

## 4. Honest limitations & scope

- The demonstrated objective is final-set **volume**; other objectives (task-direction tightness,
  control cost, inner/outer bracket) are natural but not yet run.
- The policy wins on 68% (not all) of held-out systems and captures ~half the oracle gap — it is a
  *useful amortization*, not a replacement for per-instance optimization when that is affordable.
- Experiments are 2-D LTI with the scalar β-gauge; the π(t)/S(t) gauges of the continuous KV tube and
  higher dimensions are the immediate extensions (the theory and code structure carry over).
- This tightens a *certified outer* set; it is orthogonal to the inner/robust results of paper-4.

## 5. Related work and precise novelty

- **Learned template *directions*** — adaptive polytopes ([Entesari & Fazlyab, arXiv:2212.07553]),
  PCA templates ([ReachLipBnB, arXiv:2211.00608]): learn *which directions* to bound a polytope/support
  set along. We instead learn the *continuous shape-evolution gauge* of an ellipsoidal tube — a
  different object with no polytope analog.
- **Reach-set synthesis as optimal control** ([iterative-DP terminal-volume, arXiv:2509.23367]):
  minimizes terminal volume for *normotopes* via DP and lists RL as *future work*. We (i) use the
  ellipsoid-specific gauge, (ii) *implement* an amortized learned policy, and (iii) make the
  soundness-for-any-θ invariant explicit.
- **Reach-SDP** ([arXiv:2004.07876]): re-solves an SDP per instance for an ellipsoidal outer set; we
  amortize via a learned gauge policy (single forward pass online) and exploit the tube gauge, not SDP.
- **Differentiable robust MPC** ([arXiv:2308.08426]): tunes the *controller*; we tune the
  *reachability method's internal gauge*.

**Precise novelty:** learning a policy that lives entirely within the *soundness-preserving,
ellipsoid-specific gauge freedom* of a certified reach tube — so safety is structural and only
tightness is learned — appears not to have been done. We frame it as a methods contribution with a
soundness theorem and an amortization result, and we validate that the gauge is genuinely exploitable
(1.44× oracle, 48% captured by the learned policy) with certified soundness (1.0000).

## 6. Reproducibility

`bash paper-5/reproduce.sh` (SciPy required) regenerates `results/{gauge_gap,amortized,soundness}.csv`.
Kernel: `python/ell_gauge.py`, `python/ellreach.py`. Soundness unit-tests in
`python/oracle_tests/test_ell_gauge.py`. *All quantitative claims trace to the regenerated CSVs.*

## Appendix A — the β-family is sound for all β>0

For symmetric PSD `Q₁=AQAᵀ`, `Q_W`, and any `d`: with `p₁²=dᵀQ₁d`, `p₂²=dᵀQ_W d`,
`dᵀQ_β d = (1+1/β)p₁² + (1+β)p₂² = (p₁+p₂)² + (p₁/√β − p₂√β)² ≥ (p₁+p₂)² = (ρ(Q₁,d)+ρ(Q_W,d))²`.
Equality iff `β = p₁/p₂` (the myopic KV value for direction `d`). Thus every β>0 over-approximates the
Minkowski sum, tight along the single direction `d=d(β)`.
